questions.q: We see with our ______.
questions.e: Eyes are the sense organs that help us see.

questions.q: We hear with our ______.
questions.e: Ears help us hear sounds.

questions.q: We smell a flower with our ______.
questions.e: The nose helps us smell things.

questions.q: My father's mother is my ______.
questions.e: Father's mother is our grandmother. We call her Dadi.

questions.q: We get milk from a ______.
questions.e: Cows, buffaloes and goats give us milk.

questions.q: The part of a plant under the soil is the ______.
questions.e: Roots grow under the soil. They hold the plant.

questions.q: Most leaves are ______ in colour.
questions.e: Most leaves are green.

questions.q: A dog lives in a ______.
questions.e: A kennel is a home for a dog.

questions.q: Birds live in a ______.
questions.e: Birds make nests to live and lay eggs.

questions.q: A ______ brings letters to our home.
questions.e: The postman brings letters and parcels.

questions.q: A ______ treats us when we are sick.
questions.e: A doctor gives us medicine and helps us get well.

questions.q: We should brush our teeth ______ a day.
questions.e: Brush in the morning and at night. That is twice a day.

questions.q: We light diyas on ______.
questions.e: Diwali is the festival of lights. We light diyas.

questions.q: Holi is the festival of ______.
questions.e: On Holi we play with colours.

questions.q: Which part of the body helps us feel hot and cold?
questions.e: Our skin feels hot, cold, soft and hard.

questions.q: How many fingers are there on one hand?
questions.e: One hand has five fingers, counting the thumb.

questions.q: My mother's brother is my ______.
questions.e: Mother's brother is our uncle. We call him Mama.

questions.q: Grandparents, parents, uncles, aunts and children live together. This is a ______ family.
questions.e: A joint family has many family members living together.

questions.q: Honey is made by ______.
questions.e: Honeybees make honey from flowers.

questions.q: We get eggs from a ______.
questions.e: Hens lay eggs. We eat them.

questions.q: A big plant with a thick, hard trunk is a ______.
questions.e: Trees are big and have a thick trunk, like the mango and neem tree.

questions.q: A mango is the ______ of the mango tree.
questions.e: Mango is a fruit. It grows on the tree.

questions.q: Animals we keep at home are called ______ animals.
questions.e: Pet animals like cats and dogs live with us.

questions.q: The young one of a cow is a ______.
questions.e: A baby cow is called a calf.

questions.q: Lions and tigers live in the ______.
questions.e: Lions and tigers are wild animals. They live in forests.

questions.q: A ______ grows food for us in the fields.
questions.e: Farmers grow rice, wheat and vegetables.

questions.q: A ______ stitches our clothes.
questions.e: A tailor sews clothes for us.

questions.q: Wash your hands with ______ and water before eating.
questions.e: Soap removes dirt and germs from our hands.

questions.q: We should cross the road at the ______.
questions.e: The zebra crossing is the safe place to cross the road.

questions.q: On ______, people decorate a tree with stars and lights.
questions.e: On Christmas, people decorate a Christmas tree.

questions.q: Arjun closed his eyes. He still knew the lemon was sour. Which body part told him?
questions.e: The tongue tells us if food is sweet, sour, salty or bitter.

questions.q: Riya hears the school bell. She is using her sense of ______.
questions.e: We use the sense of hearing with our ears.

questions.q: Riya lives with her father, mother and one brother. How many people are in her family with Riya?
questions.e: Father, mother, brother and Riya make 4 people.

questions.q: Paneer is made from ______.
questions.e: Paneer is made from milk. Milk comes from animals.

questions.q: Ravi did not water his plant for many days. The plant will ______.
questions.e: Plants need water. Without water they dry up.

questions.q: Which part of a plant later becomes a fruit?
questions.e: Flowers turn into fruits. Fruits have seeds.

questions.q: Which animal gives us wool?
questions.e: Wool comes from the hair of sheep.

questions.q: A frog can live in water and on ______.
questions.e: A frog lives in water and on land.

questions.q: Meera's shoe is torn. Who will mend it?
questions.e: A cobbler mends shoes and chappals.

questions.q: The traffic light is red. What should we do?
questions.e: Red light means stop. Green light means go.

questions.q: Rohan threw a banana peel on the road. Where should he throw it?
questions.e: We should always put waste in a dustbin.

questions.q: People in Kerala make a flower rangoli called pookalam on ______.
questions.e: Onam is a festival of Kerala. People make pookalam with flowers.

questions.q: Look at your body.
p: (a) How many eyes do you have?
questions.e: We have two eyes. Legs help us walk and teeth help us chew.

questions.q: Meera lives with her Dada, Dadi, Papa, Mummy and little brother.
p: (a) How many people live in Meera's home with her?
questions.e: Dada, Dadi, Papa, Mummy, brother and Meera make 6. Dadi is Papa's mother.

questions.q: Riya's lunch box has roti, dal, an apple and a glass of milk.
p: (a) Which food in her box comes from an animal?
(b) Which food in her box is a fruit?
questions.e: Milk comes from animals. An apple is a fruit from a tree.

questions.q: Arjun planted a seed in a pot.
p: (a) What should he give the soil every day?
(b) Where should he keep the pot?
(c) What comes out of the seed first?
questions.e: Seeds need water and sunlight to grow. A tiny root comes out first.

questions.q: Look at a cow, a hen and a fish.
p: (c) How many legs does a cow have?
questions.e: A fish lives in water. A hen has 2 legs. A cow has 4 legs.

questions.q: There is a fire. Which number do we call for the fire brigade in India?
questions.e: 101 is the fire brigade number. 100 is for police.

questions.q: A stranger offers you sweets. What should you do?
questions.a: Say no and tell your parents
questions.e: Never take things from strangers. Always tell your parents or teacher.

questions.q: Festivals are fun.
p: (a) On which festival in January do we fly kites?
(b) On Raksha Bandhan, a sister ties a ______ on her brother's wrist.
questions.e: We fly kites on Makar Sankranti. Sisters tie rakhi on Raksha Bandhan.

questions.q: Rain falls from the ______.
questions.e: Rain comes from the clouds in the sky.

questions.q: Water that is safe to drink is ______ water.
questions.e: We must drink only clean, safe water.

questions.q: Moving air is called ______.
questions.e: When air moves, we call it wind.

questions.q: We need air to ______.
questions.e: All living things need air to breathe.

questions.q: We wear ______ clothes in winter.
questions.e: Woollen clothes keep us warm in winter.

questions.q: We use an umbrella or a ______ in the rain.
questions.e: A raincoat keeps us dry in the rain.

questions.q: A small house made of mud and straw is a ______.
questions.e: A hut is made of mud, straw and bamboo.

questions.q: A ______ is a house made of cloth. We can carry it.
questions.e: A tent is made of cloth. It can be folded and carried.

questions.q: An ______ flies in the sky.
questions.e: Aeroplanes and helicopters fly in the sky.

questions.q: A train runs on ______.
questions.e: Trains run on railway tracks.

questions.q: In ______ it is very hot.
questions.e: Summer is the hottest season.

questions.q: After rain we may see a ______ of seven colours in the sky.
questions.e: A rainbow has seven colours.

questions.q: We get ______ from trees to make tables and chairs.
questions.e: Wood from trees is used to make furniture.

questions.q: A fish breathes with its ______.
questions.e: Fish breathe in water with their gills.

questions.q: Water turns into ice when it is very ______.
questions.e: When water becomes very cold, it freezes into ice.

questions.q: We should ______ the tap after use to save water.
questions.e: Closing the tap stops water from going waste.

questions.q: A kite flies high because of the ______.
questions.e: Moving air lifts the kite up.

questions.q: Air fills a ______ and makes it big.
questions.e: When we blow air into a balloon, it gets bigger.

questions.q: ______ clothes keep us cool in summer.
questions.e: Cotton clothes are light and keep us cool.

questions.q: Wool comes from ______.
questions.e: Wool is made from the hair of sheep.

questions.q: Many families live in one tall building. They live in ______.
questions.e: A tall building has many flats.

questions.q: In Kashmir, some people live in a house that floats on water. It is a ______.
questions.e: Houseboats float on the Dal Lake in Srinagar.

questions.q: A ______ carries people across the sea.
questions.e: Ships and boats move on water.

questions.q: Which vehicle has two wheels and no engine?
questions.e: We pedal a bicycle. It has no engine.

questions.q: In winter, the days are ______.
questions.e: In winter the sun sets early, so days are short.

questions.q: In which season do many trees shed their leaves?
questions.e: In autumn, leaves turn yellow and fall.

questions.q: Small plants with soft green stems, like mint (pudina), are ______.
questions.e: Herbs are small plants with soft stems.

questions.q: A money plant takes support to grow up. It is a ______.
questions.e: Climbers have weak stems and need support.

questions.q: A rabbit lives in a hole under the ground. It is called a ______.
questions.e: Rabbits and rats live in burrows.

questions.q: On the road we should walk on the ______.
questions.e: The footpath is safe for people who walk.

questions.q: Riya put her wet dress in the sun. It became dry. The water went into the ______.
questions.e: The sun's heat turns water into vapour. It goes into the air.

questions.q: Sea water tastes ______.
questions.e: Sea water has a lot of salt in it.

questions.q: Arjun blows on his hot milk. Moving air makes the milk ______.
questions.e: Blowing air on hot food cools it down.

questions.q: Police, nurses and soldiers wear special clothes at work. These are called ______.
questions.e: A uniform shows the work a person does.

questions.q: Houses in places with heavy rain have ______ roofs so water slides off.
questions.e: Sloping roofs let rainwater flow down quickly.

questions.q: Houses made of bricks, cement and iron are ______ houses.
questions.e: Pucca houses are strong. They are made of bricks and cement.

questions.q: Meera wants to go from Delhi to Mumbai very fast. What should she take?
questions.e: An aeroplane is the fastest way to travel far.

questions.q: Which animal carries people and loads in the desert?
questions.e: Camels can walk on sand and live without water for days.

questions.q: Arjun wears a raincoat and carries an umbrella. Which season is it?
questions.e: We need raincoats and umbrellas in the rainy season.

questions.q: Cotton for our clothes comes from a ______.
questions.e: Cotton grows on the cotton plant.

questions.q: A cow eats only plants. Animals that eat only plants are called ______.
questions.e: Cows, goats and deer eat only plants. They are herbivores.

questions.q: Riya sees a broken electric wire on the road. What should she do?
questions.a: Not touch it and tell an adult
questions.e: Electric wires can give a shock. Stay away and tell an adult.

questions.q: Rani's village gets water from a well, a pond and a river.
p: (a) Which one is dug deep into the ground?
(b) Before drinking pond water, we must ______ it.
(c) Ponds and rivers fill up with water from the ______.
questions.e: A well is dug in the ground. Pond water must be boiled or filtered before drinking. Rain fills ponds and rivers.

questions.q: Air is all around us.
p: (b) Smoke from cars makes the air ______.
(c) Which machine moves air in a room in summer?
questions.e: We cannot see air but can feel it. Smoke makes air dirty. A fan moves air.

questions.q: Different clothes for different needs.
p: (a) Raincoats are made of ______ so water cannot go in.
questions.e: Plastic keeps water out. Light colours keep us cool. Silkworms make silk.

questions.q: Houses are of many kinds.
p: (a) A house made of ice blocks in very cold lands is an ______.
(b) In Assam, some houses are built on bamboo ______ to stay safe from floods.
questions.e: Igloos are made of ice. Houses on stilts stay above flood water.

questions.q: Arjun counts wheels.
p: (a) How many wheels does an auto-rickshaw have?
(b) How many wheels does a car have?
(c) How many wheels do two bicycles have in all?
questions.e: An auto has 3 wheels, a car has 4, and each bicycle has 2, so two bicycles have 4.

questions.q: Rahul gets a small cut on his knee. It is washed with clean water and covered with a ______.
questions.e: A clean bandage keeps dirt and germs away from a cut.

questions.q: We eat different parts of plants.
p: (a) Which part of a carrot do we eat?
(b) Which part of spinach (palak) do we eat?
(c) Which part of sugarcane do we eat?
questions.e: Carrot is a root, palak gives us leaves and sugarcane is a stem.

questions.q: A tiger eats other animals. Animals that eat only flesh are called ______.
questions.e: Tigers and lions eat flesh. They are carnivores.

questions.q: The mother of your mother is your ______.
questions.e: Mother's mother is our maternal grandmother, Nani.

questions.q: Your father's sister is your ______.
questions.e: Father's sister is called Bua; mother's sister is Mausi.

questions.q: A famous fair where camels are bought and sold is held every year at ______ in Rajasthan.
questions.e: The Pushkar Mela in Rajasthan is famous for its camel fair.

questions.q: Pongal is a harvest festival mainly celebrated in ______.
questions.e: Pongal is the harvest festival of Tamil Nadu, when new rice is cooked with milk and jaggery.

questions.q: Plants of medium height with hard stems and many branches near the ground, like rose and hibiscus, are called ______.
questions.e: Shrubs are bushy plants with woody stems, smaller than trees.

questions.q: The ______ of a plant holds it firmly in the soil.
questions.e: Roots grow into the soil, hold the plant and take in water.

questions.q: A squirrel often makes its home in a ______.
questions.a: tree|trees|tree hole|hollow of a tree|tree hollow
questions.e: Squirrels live in trees and make nests in holes or between branches.

questions.q: Most of the water on Earth is in the ______.
questions.e: Oceans and seas hold most of the Earth's water, but it is salty.

questions.q: Rice, wheat, maize and bajra are called ______.
questions.e: Cereals are grains that give us energy.

questions.q: Dal is made from ______.
questions.e: Moong, masoor, arhar and chana are pulses used to make dal.

questions.q: We should drink plenty of clean ______ every day.
questions.e: Clean water keeps our body healthy.

questions.q: A potter makes pots from ______.
questions.e: A potter shapes wet clay on a wheel and bakes it.

questions.q: Vegetable peels and leftover food are ______ waste.
questions.e: Wet waste comes from the kitchen and rots easily.

questions.q: Dry waste like paper and plastic goes in the ______ dustbin.
questions.e: In India, the green bin is for wet waste and the blue bin is for dry waste.

questions.q: A family with only parents and their children is called a ______ family.
questions.e: A nuclear family has parents and their children only.

questions.q: People who live in the houses next to ours are our ______.
questions.e: Neighbours live near us and help each other.

questions.q: At a mela, Arjun buys 3 balloons at ₹5 each. How much does he pay in rupees?
questions.e: 3 × 5 = 15, so he pays ₹15.

questions.q: The big round ride at a mela that takes people high up is called a ______.
questions.e: A giant wheel turns slowly and lifts people high above the ground.

questions.q: Bihu is celebrated in ______.
questions.e: Bihu is the festival of Assam, celebrated with Bihu dance.

questions.q: On Onam, people in Kerala enjoy a big feast served on banana leaves called ______.
questions.e: The Onam sadya has many dishes served on a banana leaf.

questions.q: The thin lines on a leaf are called ______.
questions.e: Veins carry water and food in the leaf.

questions.q: The ______ carries water from the roots to the leaves.
questions.e: The stem holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves.

questions.q: Bees collect sweet ______ from flowers to make honey.
questions.e: Bees suck nectar from flowers and turn it into honey.

questions.q: The weaver bird (baya) makes its hanging nest by weaving ______.
questions.e: The baya weaves strips of grass and leaves into a hanging nest.

questions.q: An old well with steps going down to the water is called a ______.
questions.e: Stepwells (baolis) were built long ago to store water, like Rani ki Vav in Gujarat.

questions.q: Dirty water can cause diseases like ______.
questions.e: Germs in dirty water cause diarrhoea, cholera and typhoid.

questions.q: Mango, banana and guava are ______.
questions.e: Mango, banana and guava are fruits that grow on plants.

questions.q: Playing outdoor games like kho-kho keeps our body ______.
questions.e: Exercise and play make our body fit and strong.

questions.q: A ______ makes tables and doors from wood.
questions.e: A carpenter cuts and joins wood to make furniture.

questions.q: Old newspapers and plastic bottles are sent to factories to make new things. This is called ______.
questions.e: Recycling turns old waste into new things.

questions.q: Riya lives with her 2 grandparents, 2 parents, 1 uncle, 1 aunt and 2 cousins. How many people live in the house including Riya?
questions.e: 2 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 8, and Riya makes 9.

questions.q: Meera has ₹50. At the mela she buys bangles for ₹20 and a toy for ₹15. How many rupees are left?
Christmas is celebrated on ______ December.
questions.e: Christmas falls on 25 December every year.

questions.q: Arjun put seeds in two pots. He watered only pot A. In which pot will the seeds sprout?
questions.e: Seeds need water to sprout. The dry pot will not show sprouts.

questions.q: Banana leaves are big and broad. Pine leaves are thin and ______-shaped.
questions.e: Pine trees in the hills have thin, needle-shaped leaves.

questions.q: A peepal tree gives shelter to birds and squirrels, and birds spread its seeds. So plants and animals ______ each other.
questions.e: Plants give animals food and shelter; animals help plants spread seeds and pollen.

questions.q: A tap leaks 1 drop every second. 20 drops make 1 mL. How many mL of water are wasted in 1 minute?
questions.e: 1 minute = 60 drops; 60 ÷ 20 = 3 mL.

questions.q: Which is a good way to save water while brushing teeth?
questions.a: Turn off the tap while brushing
questions.e: Closing the tap while brushing saves many litres of water.

questions.q: Riya's plate has roti, dal, rice, sabzi and curd. Which item is made from milk?
questions.e: Curd (dahi) is made by setting milk.

questions.q: When Rohan sneezes, he should cover his nose and mouth with a ______ or his elbow.
questions.e: Covering a sneeze stops germs from spreading to others.

questions.q: A blacksmith makes tools like sickles and axes from ______.
questions.e: A blacksmith heats iron and beats it into shape.

questions.q: Riya has old newspapers, a plastic bottle and a banana peel. Which one goes in the green bin?
questions.e: The banana peel is wet waste, so it goes in the green bin.

questions.q: Arjun's family photo shows Dadaji, Dadiji, Papa, Mummy, Chacha, Chachi, Arjun and his sister Tara.
p: (a) What type of family is this?
questions.e: Many generations living together make a joint family. Chacha is father's brother and Tara is her grandfather's granddaughter.

questions.q: Look at a mango tree.
p: (a) What is the thick, hard stem of a tree called?
(b) Which part makes food for the plant using sunlight?
(c) Where is the mango seed found?
questions.e: A tree has a woody trunk. Leaves make food with sunlight. The seed is inside the fruit.

questions.q: In Meera's garden there are bees, a crow's nest and earthworms in the soil.
p: (a) Which insect in the garden makes honey?
(b) Which black bird builds a nest of twigs high in trees?
(c) Earthworms make the soil soft and ______ for plants.
questions.e: Bees make honey, crows build twig nests, and earthworms loosen and enrich the soil.

questions.q: A family uses 50 L water for bathing, 30 L for washing clothes and 20 L for cooking and drinking in a day.
p: (a) How many litres do they use in all?
(b) How many more litres are used for bathing than for cooking and drinking?
(c) Collecting and storing rainwater for later use is called rainwater ______.
questions.e: 50 + 30 + 20 = 100 L; 50 − 20 = 30 L. Rainwater harvesting helps save water.

questions.q: Food is cooked in different ways.
p: (a) Rice is cooked by ______ it in water.
(b) Puris are cooked by ______ in hot oil.
questions.e: Rice is boiled, puris are fried, and rotis are made from wheat flour (atta).

questions.q: Meera ate uncovered food from a stall and fell sick. Flies that sit on uncovered food spread ______.
questions.e: Flies carry germs from dirt to food. Always eat covered, clean food.

questions.q: Khadi cloth is woven from yarn spun by hand on a ______.
questions.e: Gandhiji made the charkha a symbol of making our own cloth (khadi).

questions.q: Let us take charge of waste.
p: (b) Using an old jam jar as a pencil stand is called ______.
(c) Kitchen waste rots in a pit and becomes manure called ______.
questions.e: Reduce, Reuse and Recycle help cut waste. Wet waste can be turned into compost.

questions.q: In Kerala, some children cross the backwaters to school in a small boat called a ______.
questions.e: A vallam is a small wooden boat used in the backwaters of Kerala.

questions.q: In Assam, children often cross streams on bridges made of ______.
questions.e: Bamboo bridges are common in Assam, where many streams and rivers flow.

questions.q: Animals whose ears can be seen from outside have ______ or fur on their bodies.
questions.e: Animals with outer ears, like cows and dogs, have hair or fur on their bodies.

questions.q: Birds have ear ______ but no outer ears.
questions.e: Birds hear through small ear holes hidden under their feathers.

questions.q: An elephant herd is led by the oldest ______ elephant.
questions.e: The oldest female elephant leads the herd.

questions.q: Amrita Devi belonged to the ______ community.
questions.e: The Bishnoi community is known for protecting trees and animals.

questions.q: Amrita Devi's village, Khejadli, is in ______.
questions.e: Khejadli is a village near Jodhpur in Rajasthan.

questions.q: Keeping bees to get honey is called ______.
questions.e: Anita learnt beekeeping and sold honey to earn money.

questions.t: Hu Tu Tu, Hu Tu Tu
questions.q: Hu Tu Tu is another name for the game ______.
questions.e: Kabaddi is also called Hu Tu Tu in some parts of India.

questions.q: Carrot and radish are ______ that we eat.
questions.e: Carrot, radish and turnip are roots that store food.

questions.q: Silk thread is taken from the ______ of the silkworm.
questions.e: The silkworm spins a cocoon of silk thread around itself.

questions.q: The money used in a country is called its ______.
questions.e: Every country has its own currency, like the rupee in India.

questions.q: Which spice turns dal and sabzi yellow?
questions.e: Turmeric (haldi) gives food its yellow colour.

questions.q: The banyan tree has roots hanging down from its branches. These are ______ roots.
questions.e: The banyan's hanging (aerial/prop) roots grow down to the soil and support its huge branches.

questions.q: In some hilly places, children cross a river by sitting in a ______ that slides along a strong rope or wire.
questions.e: A trolley pulled along a steel rope helps people cross rivers where there is no bridge.

questions.q: An elephant flaps its big ears to ______ itself.
questions.e: Elephants flap their ears like fans to cool their bodies.

questions.q: Which of these animals has ears that can be seen from outside: elephant, crow, lizard or snake?
questions.e: An elephant has big outer ears. Crows and lizards have only ear holes; snakes have no outer ears.

questions.q: Male elephants leave the herd when they are about how many years old?
questions.e: Young male elephants leave the herd at about 14–15 years of age.

questions.q: Elephants love to roll in ______ to keep their skin cool.
questions.e: A mud bath keeps the elephant's skin cool and protects it.

questions.q: An elephant can eat about how many kilograms of leaves and twigs in a day?
questions.e: An elephant eats about 100 kg of leaves and twigs every day.

questions.q: The people of Khejadli gave their lives to save ______ trees.
questions.e: The Bishnois hugged the khejadi trees to stop them from being cut.

questions.q: How many people gave their lives to save the trees of Khejadli?
questions.e: 363 Bishnoi men, women and children gave their lives along with Amrita Devi.

questions.q: Anita lives in Bochaha village in Muzaffarpur district of ______.
questions.e: Muzaffarpur in Bihar is famous for litchis and honey.

questions.q: Honey from Muzaffarpur is famous because the bees collect nectar from ______ flowers.
questions.e: Bees visit litchi orchards there, so the honey is called litchi honey.

questions.t: Hu Tu Tu, Hu Tu Tu
questions.q: In a kabaddi match, how many players does each team have on the court?
questions.e: Each kabaddi team has 7 players on the court.

questions.q: Roots take in ______ from the soil.
questions.e: Roots absorb water and minerals from the soil for the plant.

questions.q: Silkworms feed on the leaves of the ______ tree.
questions.e: Silkworms eat mulberry leaves and then spin cocoons.

questions.q: Pochampalli is famous for its tie-and-dye silk sarees called ______ sarees.
questions.e: In ikat, threads are tied and dyed before weaving to make patterns.

questions.q: The currency of Bangladesh is the ______.
questions.e: Bangladesh uses the taka.

questions.q: Cinnamon (dalchini) is the ______ of a tree.
questions.e: Cinnamon is the dried inner bark of a tree.

questions.q: Rafiq's school is across a river with no bridge. Name one thing that can help him cross.
questions.e: Where there is no bridge, children cross rivers by boat or trolley.

questions.q: An animal has ear holes but no outer ears, and its body is covered with feathers. What kind of animal is it?
questions.e: Feathers and ear holes without outer ears are signs of a bird.

questions.q: One elephant eats 100 kg of leaves in a day. How many kg will 3 elephants eat in 2 days?
The men who came to cut the trees of Khejadli were sent by the king of ______.
questions.e: The king of Jodhpur needed wood for his new palace.

questions.q: An award for protecting wildlife is given today in the name of ______.
questions.e: The Amrita Devi Bishnoi Award honours people who protect wildlife.

questions.q: In a beehive, the only bee that lays eggs is the ______ bee.
questions.e: The queen bee lays all the eggs; worker bees collect nectar and look after the hive.

questions.t: Hu Tu Tu, Hu Tu Tu
questions.q: In kabaddi, the raider must touch players of the other team while holding his ______.
questions.e: The raider keeps saying 'kabaddi' in one breath while trying to touch the opponents.

questions.q: Abdul kept moong seeds on wet cotton. The tiny white part that grows downward from the seed becomes the ______.
questions.e: When a seed sprouts, the root grows down and the shoot grows up.

questions.q: To get silk thread, the cocoons are put in ______ water.
questions.e: Cocoons are boiled in hot water to loosen the silk thread.

questions.q: Riya's uncle lives in the USA. Which currency does he use there?
questions.e: The USA uses the dollar.

questions.q: The symbol ₹ stands for the Indian ______.
questions.e: ₹ is the symbol of the Indian rupee.

questions.q: Cloves (laung) are dried flower ______.
questions.e: Cloves are the flower buds of the clove tree, picked and dried.

questions.q: An elephant herd has 12 elephants. Three of them are young males who are now 15 years old.
p: (a) What will the young males now do?
(b) How many elephants will stay in the herd?
(c) The herd is made up of female elephants and their ______.
questions.e: Male elephants leave the herd at 14–15 years. 12 − 3 = 9. A herd has females and their young.

questions.q: Think about the story of Amrita.
p: (a) What did Amrita Devi do to stop the men from cutting the tree?
hugged it|hugged the tree|hugged|hug|clung to it
(b) About how many years ago did this happen?
questions.e: About 300 years ago, Amrita Devi hugged the khejadi tree to protect it.

questions.q: A beekeeper has 5 bee boxes. Each box gives 4 kg of honey.
p: (a) How many kg of honey does she get in all?
(b) She sells it at ₹200 per kg. How many rupees does she earn?
(c) The bees that fly out to collect nectar are called ______ bees.
questions.e: 5 × 4 = 20 kg; 20 × 200 = ₹4000. Worker bees collect nectar.

questions.q: Abdul sees heavy rain wash soil away from a bare field, but not from his garden full of plants.
p: (a) Which part of the plant holds the soil and stops it from being washed away?
(b) Through which part does water go up from the roots to the leaves?
questions.e: Roots bind the soil, and the stem carries water up to the leaves.

questions.q: Arjun's friends live in Japan, the UK and Nepal.
p: (a) What is the currency of Japan?
(b) What is the currency of the UK?
(c) What is the currency of Nepal?
questions.e: Japan uses the yen, the UK the pound and Nepal the Nepalese rupee.

questions.q: Pochampalli, the village of weavers, is in the state of ______.
questions.e: Pochampalli is in Nalgonda district, now in Telangana (earlier Andhra Pradesh).

questions.q: In India, saffron (kesar) is mostly grown in ______.
questions.e: Saffron is grown mainly in the Pampore area of Kashmir.

questions.q: Shabnam cycles 3 km to school and 3 km back every day. How many km does she cycle in 6 school days?
questions.e: Each day 3 + 3 = 6 km; 6 × 6 = 36 km.

questions.q: An ant finds its way by following the ______ left by other ants.
questions.e: Ants leave a smell on the path; other ants follow it.

questions.q: Owls can see very well at ______.
questions.e: Owls have big eyes that help them see in the dark.

questions.q: Snake charmers play a wind instrument called the ______.
questions.e: The been (pungi) is made from a dried gourd.

questions.q: We taste sweet, sour, salty and bitter with our ______.
questions.e: Different parts of the tongue help us sense different tastes.

questions.q: Coconut seeds are spread by ______.
questions.e: Coconuts can float and are carried by water to new places.

questions.q: The Ghadsisar lake is in ______, Rajasthan.
questions.e: Ghadsisar lake in Jaisalmer was built to collect rainwater.

questions.q: Malaria is spread by the female ______ mosquito.
questions.e: The female Anopheles mosquito spreads malaria.

questions.q: Mosquitoes lay eggs in ______ water.
questions.e: Mosquitoes breed in water that stays still, as in coolers, pots and puddles.

questions.q: The Golconda fort is in ______.
questions.e: Golconda fort stands on a hill in Hyderabad.

questions.q: Sunita Williams is an ______ who has travelled into space.
questions.e: Sunita Williams is an astronaut of Indian origin.

questions.q: From space, the Earth looks ______.
questions.e: The Earth is round like a ball.

questions.q: The Changpa people live in the ______ area of Ladakh.
questions.e: Changthang is a high, cold area of Ladakh.

questions.q: The Bhuj earthquake took place in ______.
questions.e: Bhuj is in the Kutch district of Gujarat.

questions.q: During an earthquake, we should hide under a strong ______.
questions.e: A strong table protects us from falling things: drop, cover and hold.

questions.q: A sloth sleeps for about how many hours a day?
questions.e: The sloth sleeps about 17 hours a day, hanging upside down from trees.

questions.q: A mosquito finds people by the ______ of their sweat and body heat.
questions.e: Mosquitoes find us by the smell of our sweat and our body heat.

questions.q: Snake charmers belong to the ______ community.
questions.e: The Kalbelia community traditionally kept snakes and played the been.

questions.q: Snakes cannot hear the been. They sway by watching its ______.
questions.e: Snakes have no outer ears; they follow the movement of the been.

questions.q: If we chew a roti for a long time, it begins to taste ______.
questions.e: Saliva changes starch in the roti into sugar, so it tastes sweet.

questions.q: The watery juice in our mouth that softens food is ______.
questions.e: Saliva makes food wet and soft and starts digestion.

questions.q: Chillies were brought to India long ago from ______.
questions.e: Chillies came to India from South America with traders.

questions.q: Light, hairy seeds like those of cotton and aak (madar) are spread by ______.
questions.e: Hairy seeds are light and float away in the wind.

questions.q: In Rajasthan, rainwater is stored in covered underground tanks called ______.
questions.e: Kunds have a sloping catchment that guides rainwater into a covered tank.

questions.q: Ghadsisar lake was built by King ______.
questions.e: Maharawal Ghadsi built the lake about 650 years ago; the people helped.

questions.q: The scientist who found out that mosquitoes spread malaria was ______.
questions.e: Ronald Ross did this work in India and won the Nobel Prize in 1902.

questions.q: A ______ at the gate of Golconda fort can be heard at the very top of the fort.
questions.e: The fort was built so that a clap at the gate could be heard at the top, to warn of danger.

questions.q: Golconda fort was made into a great fort by the ______ kings.
questions.e: The Qutub Shahi kings ruled from Golconda about 400 years ago.

questions.q: The first Indian to go into space was ______.
questions.e: Rakesh Sharma went into space in 1984.

questions.q: The tents of the Changpa are called ______.
questions.e: A rebo is a tent the Changpa can carry as they move.

questions.q: The Changpa rear ______ goats that give very fine, soft wool.
questions.e: Pashmina goats give the soft wool used to make pashmina shawls.

questions.q: Dogs mark their area by leaving their ______, which other dogs can smell.
questions.e: Dogs urinate at places to mark their area; other dogs smell it.

questions.q: There are many kinds of snakes in India. How many of them are poisonous, as told in the chapter?
questions.e: Only four are poisonous: cobra, common krait, Russell's viper and saw-scaled viper.

questions.q: The medicine made from snake poison to treat snakebite is called ______.
questions.e: Snake poison is used to make antivenom, which saves people bitten by snakes.

questions.q: Dr Beaumont learnt about digestion by studying a hole in the stomach of ______.
questions.a: Alexis St. Martin|Alexis St Martin|Alexis|St. Martin|Alexis Saint Martin
questions.e: Alexis St. Martin was shot in the stomach; the wound left a hole through which Beaumont studied digestion.

questions.q: A child with loose motions loses water. He is given clean water with sugar and salt. This drink is called ______.
questions.e: ORS (sugar + salt + water) replaces the water and salts the body loses.

questions.q: After walking in a field, Arjun found seeds stuck to his socks. Such seeds are spread by ______.
questions.e: Hooked seeds stick to fur and clothes and are carried to new places.

questions.q: A family uses 30 litres of water a day from its kund. How many days will 900 litres last?
In malaria, the fever often comes with ______ (feeling very cold and shaking).
questions.e: Malaria fever comes with shivering, and it may come back on alternate days.

questions.q: Golconda was famous long ago for the trade in ______.
questions.e: Golconda was a big market for diamonds mined nearby.

questions.q: In a spaceship, things float because there is almost no ______ pulling them down.
questions.e: On Earth, gravity pulls things down; in space they feel weightless and float.

questions.q: The Changpa's rebo is made from the hair of the ______.
questions.e: Yak hair is woven into strips that are sewn together to make the rebo.

questions.q: The Bhuj earthquake happened on 26 January of which year?
questions.e: The Gujarat earthquake struck on 26 January 2001.

questions.q: Different animals have super senses.
p: (a) Which bird turns its head almost all the way round because it cannot move its eyes?
(b) Which animal flies in the dark by listening to the echo of its own sounds?
(c) A male silk moth can smell a female moth from many ______ away.
questions.e: Owls turn their heads, bats use echoes, and moths have a very strong sense of smell.

questions.q: Riya kept moong seeds dry in bowl A and on wet cotton in bowl B.
p: (a) In which bowl will the seeds sprout?
(b) Besides water, what do seeds need to sprout?
(c) 15 of the 20 seeds sprouted. How many did not sprout?
questions.e: Seeds need water and air to sprout. 20 − 15 = 5.

questions.q: A school collects rainwater from its roof into a tank of 5000 litres. It uses 250 litres a day.
p: (a) How many days will a full tank last?
(b) Collecting rainwater like this is called rainwater ______.
questions.e: 5000 ÷ 250 = 20 days. Rainwater harvesting saves water for dry days.

questions.q: Ravi has a high fever with shivering.
p: (a) To check for malaria, the doctor tests his ______.
(b) Name another disease spread by mosquitoes that causes high fever and body pain.
(c) Which oil is spread on stagnant water to kill mosquito larvae?
questions.e: A blood test shows malaria. Dengue is also spread by mosquitoes. Kerosene on water kills larvae.

questions.q: Your building starts shaking in an earthquake.
p: (a) Should you use the lift or the stairs?
(b) After coming out, you should go to an open ______ away from buildings.
questions.e: Lifts may stop in an earthquake, so use the stairs. Open ground is safe from falling walls.

questions.q: Think about space and the Earth.
p: (a) Kalpana Chawla, the astronaut, was born in which Indian state?
(b) The line where the Earth and the sky seem to meet is called the ______.
questions.e: Kalpana Chawla was born in Karnal, Haryana. The horizon is where land and sky seem to meet.

questions.q: A deep ditch filled with water around a fort to keep enemies away is called a ______.
questions.e: A moat made it hard for enemies to reach the fort walls.

questions.q: The Changpa move from place to place with their animals in search of grass. People who live like this are called ______.
questions.e: Nomads move with their herds to find fresh grass.
